name: orient
description: START HERE. Returns everything needed to use SandboxAPIs with no docs: the universe/theme, every API surface and its base URL (git hosts and issue trackers), live-vs-snapshot modes and how to pin, the org and its teams/repos, notable entry points (each with a ready-to-run REST path), where the coverage manifest lives, and this server's access block: whether a key is set and how many requests are left this hour. Writes: this server is READ-ONLY, including for a scratch-enabled key. The scratch layer (a per-key, 24-hour overlay: GitHub issues and issue comments, Jira comments and transitions, and Slack messages into existing channels) is a REST feature, so use the GitHub, Jira or Slack base URL above with your key for it, and expect the tools here to answer from the shared data set alone.

name: check_budget
description: Costs nothing. Call it before any loop of more than a handful of requests. Returns this server's real hourly window (limit, remaining, when it resets) read from the provider's own budget endpoint, which is exempt from the budget it reports, plus whether a key is set and where to raise the limit. The window is ONE bucket per caller shared across every provider host, so the numbers apply to all of them.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The provider host you are about to call, one of the ids orient lists, e.g. 'github'. Optional: the budget is one shared window, so the numbers are the same for every provider.

name: list_repositories
description: List repositories for the universe's org. Results are identical to the provider's REST API and carry provider-form ids (node_id / numeric id).

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host to list repositories from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', e.g. 'github'.

name: get_repository
description: Fetch one repository by name (default: the flagship repo). Provider-shaped, with provider-form ids.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host to read the repository from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', e.g. 'github'.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.desc: The repository name without the organisation, e.g. 'parthenon', the flagship repo, which is used when omitted.

name: list_pull_requests
description: List a repo's pull requests (GitHub) or merge requests (GitLab). Optional state filter.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host to read from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', e.g. 'gitlab' for merge requests.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.desc: The repository name without the organisation, e.g. 'parthenon', the flagship repo, which is used when omitted.

arguments.name: state
arguments.desc: Filter by state, one of 'open', 'closed', 'merged' or 'all', e.g. 'merged'; when omitted the provider's own default applies.

name: get_pull_request
description: Fetch one PR (GitHub) / MR (GitLab) plus its reviews (GitHub) / approvals (GitLab). Returns both in one result; each carries provider-form ids for cross-referencing.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host to read from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', e.g. 'github'.

arguments.name: number
arguments.desc: The pull request number as the provider shows it (the merge request iid on GitLab), a positive integer, e.g. 47.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.desc: The repository name without the organisation, e.g. 'parthenon', the flagship repo, which is used when omitted.

name: list_issues
description: List a repo's issues. Optional state filter (open/closed/all).

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The provider to read issues from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github' or 'gitlab' (per repository), or 'jira' or 'linear' (across the whole tracker), e.g. 'jira'.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.desc: The repository name without the organisation, e.g. 'parthenon', the flagship repo, which is used when omitted; ignored by 'jira' and 'linear'.

arguments.name: state
arguments.desc: Filter by state, one of 'open', 'closed' or 'all', e.g. 'closed'; when omitted the provider's own default applies.

name: get_user
description: Fetch a user by login/username. Provider-shaped, with provider-form ids.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host to read the user from, one of the ids orient lists: 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', e.g. 'github'.

arguments.name: login
arguments.desc: The user's login (GitHub) or username (GitLab), e.g. 'athena'.

name: search_commits_by_author
description: Find commits authored by a given login in a repo. Returns SHAs (identical across GitHub and GitLab, invariant #5) with a REST path to fetch each, so you can cross-reference against either provider.

arguments.name: author
arguments.desc: The author's login, matched without regard to case, e.g. 'athena'.

arguments.name: repo
arguments.desc: The repository name without the organisation, e.g. 'parthenon', the flagship repo, which is used when omitted.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The git host whose REST path each returned commit carries, 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket' or 'ado', defaulting to 'github'; commits are read from GitHub either way, because the SHAs are identical on every host.

name: get_snapshot
description: Return the pinned, reproducible hostname for a provider. Point your client's base URL at it for drift-free CI. A snapshot regenerates byte-identically on every request.

arguments.name: provider
arguments.desc: The provider to pin, one of the ids orient lists, e.g. 'github'; the newest frozen generation for it is returned, with any older ones listed beside it.
